answers.q1: pip inside a venv, driven by the repo's shell scripts (no uv, poetry or similar). Install dependencies with: scripts/install. It creates ./venv with python3 and runs pip install -U pip, then pip install -r requirements.txt. To pick a different interpreter, run: scripts/install -p python3.12
answers.q2: scripts/test. This runs scripts/check first when not on GitHub Actions, then 'coverage run -m pytest', then scripts/coverage, which enforces 100% coverage. If you only want pytest without lint or coverage, run: venv/bin/pytest
answers.q3: venv/bin/pytest tests/client/test_auth.py. The venv/bin/ prefix is needed because scripts/install puts the tools in ./venv. If you have activated the venv, plain 'pytest tests/client/test_auth.py' works. You can also run: scripts/test tests/client/test_auth.py. That passes the path through to pytest, but it also runs scripts/check and scripts/coverage, and the 100% coverage gate will fail on a partial run.
answers.q4: scripts/check. This is what CI runs ('Run linting checks' in .github/workflows/test-suite.yml). It runs ./scripts/sync-version, then venv/bin/ruff format httpx tests --diff, then venv/bin/mypy httpx tests, then venv/bin/ruff check httpx tests. To auto-fix instead of just checking, run scripts/lint.
answers.q5: I found no vendored code and no files marked generated or 'do not edit'. Do not hand-edit these build and cache outputs, all of which are gitignored: build/, dist/, site/ (built docs), htmlcov/, *.egg-info/, venv*/, .coverage, .pytest_cache/, .mypy_cache/, __pycache__/. One more constraint: the version in httpx/__version__.py must match the latest release entry in CHANGELOG.md, because scripts/sync-version checks this.
